newsitem.title: USA: Duramed to appeal FDA decision on Premarin.
newsitem.headline: Duramed to appeal FDA decision on Premarin.

text.p: Duramed Pharmaceuticals Inc said Thursday it plans to appeal the decision by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to alter its position on the required ingredients of generic versions of Premarin.
The company, which said it would file papers next week, issued the statement in response to an article that appeared in the June 5 edition of Newsday.
The article said the FDA appeared to have engaged "in political backscratching" last month when it announced it would not approve the generic because it lacked an estrogen, DHES, found in Premarin.

It also said that the FDA found in 1995 that DHES was an impurity, but reversed its stance after hearing testimony about the generic from groups that received contributions from American Home Products Corp unit Wyeth-Ayerst Laboratories, which makes Premarin.
The piece also contended an internal FDA memo dated May 3, two days before the FDA decision was announced, supported the generic, saying DHES was not a necessary component.
FDA spokesman Don McLearn told Reuters he had not seen the Newsday piece, adding he was not aware of such a May 3 memo.
"There are clearly people who disagree with this decision within the FDA," he said, adding he would therefore not be surprised if someone within the agency had written the memo.
McLearn added it was normal for both sides of any drug debate to lobby their positions. "The queston is did it have any effect on decision-making at FDA. I say 'No,'" he added.
